title: An in-flight failure must not silently erase the newest pending request

source.independentSuite: 11/11 PASS on Node v24.22.1; the failing interleaving was not covered by those 11 checks

trigger: A draw for revision r1 is in flight, revision r2 arrives and becomes the newest pending request, then the r1 draw rejects before r2 is evaluated.

observedCounterexample.cause: LatestFrameScheduler.run() catch clears this.pending and rejects every waiter, including the later revision.

mustNeverRepeat: Treat a manual later restart as proof that a request already pending at failure time was preserved.
Clear the newest pending revision without returning an explicit dropped/retry-required identity.
Reject waiters for revisions newer than the failed evaluation without distinguishing their coverage.
Use coalescing success tests or a clean restart test as substitutes for failure-interleaving coverage.
requiredEvidence: exact scheduler commit and source blob
deterministic interleaving with r1 in flight, r2 pending, then forced r1 failure
revision-scoped settlement for both r1 and r2
proof that r2 is either evaluated automatically or returned explicitly as RETRY_REQUIRED with its revision identity
proof that a stale completion cannot publish over a newer requested revision
new dispatch-time run bound to the corrected commit

gateLogic.pass: After the forced r1 failure, r2 is not silently lost: it is evaluated, or the caller receives an explicit revision-bound retry requirement and demonstrably reissues it.
gateLogic.hold: r2 disappears, is rejected only with r1's undifferentiated error, or the test observes only a later manual fresh request.
gateLogic.browserBoundary: Module-level passage does not prove browser, WebGPU, whole-player, frame-rate, or image fidelity.

appliesTo: KaoPu Engine latest-frame and newest-request schedulers
Other Mother schedulers only after a local bounded trial confirms equivalent request and failure semantics
